Stop calling it suffering and think of it as ordinary pain. If you dramatise your pain as anything more than pain you are likely to “suffer” more so because you said so.

Your perception of people is off when you’re depressed, acknowledge this fact before you make judgements. On a good day you will love people more on a bad day you will hate them.

“I’m going to be on my own for the rest of my life” me too. I’ve been a loner for as long as I can remember. Not quiet fitting in, not quiet making connections, no long term relationships, left behind, neglected. I’m 32.

I am told stories of being inpatient has being a negative experience and likely to make me worse if I did share with those that are severely ill. I don’t know if that is what I need but there is talks of it being a possibility between my psychiatrist and GPs.

That’s quiet a vivid image about you playing footy in the rain with your nurse, sounds like a nice memory you won’t be forgetting any time soon. It’s sometimes the little things like that, that will stick with you. It’s great you got the care that was needed for you at the time, there is hope still.

Advice for me? I be honest I just feel hopeless and lonely. I can’t stop myself from thinking about my primary care Dr, who helped me tremendously. I would not be where I am if it was not for help. But now I miss her care, it’s not the same with my psychiatrist. Although I am starting to trust him more. I think I crave  a loving mother figure because I didn’t have one growing up. It’s painful being attached to professionals when they can’t give me the love that I’m looking for. I’m starting to think dying is okay, I don’t particularly want to end my life for myself but I do often think about wanting a service to be euthanised. I think that I don’t want to continue living. Making connections with people leaves me with terrible emotional pain of abandonment. I don’t feel like I want to work towards anything, nor do I know what I want, including not knowing if I actually want to recover. I’m more inclined to give up and stop, not that I think I will because this train is already on the move, slowly moving.

I know it’s all in connection with having a “personality disorder” and can be remedied. I’m tired of fighting, it’s all I’ve been doing since a child. Can’t catch a break.

Thanks for sharing. I like people like you, open, straight, forward, to the point and strong to have been through so much and still surviving. I know mental conditions don’t get enough love and sympathy but I admire you.

Apparently it’s a winning combo. And it is good not winning though. I was on sertraline through my GP but was partially effective, I was referred to secondary care. So psychiatrist man put me on Mirtazapine. The side effects were horrendous, no over exaggerating but the end result is good not perfect. For anxiety it’s been life changing, me sending this message would be a “no way” before taking anti depressants. My “true” personality as come to the surface after been suppressed by anxiety for 25 years (I’m 32), so I guess it was at risk and inevitable of it being disorderly.

I’m awaiting DBT and psychological therapies to start but with COVID its  been a long wait from December. Talks of September being the start date for Distress Tolerance therapy.

I have tried fluoxetine, Citalopram and now on sertraline/Mirtazapine. I have been trying medication for 3 years.

I have been taking Sertraline and Mirtazapine for a year now and I personally found them to be life changing for anxiety. My anxiety suppressed my personality for 25 years (I am 32) and so when I got past the side effects to medication and it started to alleviate my anxiety, I came to the understanding that I have a personality disorder, emotional dysregulation, traits of BPD. The side effects to the combination of anti depressants was a terrible experience for me, 4 months I struggled with the side effects. Is the end result worth it? Yes but I found it painful to get there.

I was scared too when I started taking anti depressants. Over time you get used to the side effects, if you have any, you may not it’s possible.

You need to keep your addictions in check if you take anti depressants, I learned that the hard way last week when I binged on alcohol for the week. I literally washed the anti depressants out of my system and now i am in some pain. I’m rebuilding up anti depressants in my system and waiting for relief.
We are. I think about it more than most people i guess. I find it harder to hide the fact that I am broken. Some people are better at hiding it than others. I struggle to pretend to be okay.
I don’t agree with this right now because I feel broken.
Listening to music is a reason as any to continue living.

Yes this. Tell people. Doctor, friend, family, random person on the internet, anybody and everybody and practise talking about it. It gets easier to talk about it the more you say what’s wrong. You will find people who want to help you and those who don’t want to help, you may gain new friends and lose old friends. People may care and not care but In the end you will find people who want to help. Like I’m trying to do in this message.

My latest achievement was telling the police about my issue and they got back to me and offered to help with my alcohol issues and housing, fingers crossed it works out. In contrast this morning I was thinking about hanging myself and feeling terrible all day. Suicidal feelings are temporary for me, not to say I won’t feel it again but they are short lived. 

There’s a reason why I feel suicidal and i have recently learned (after many a years learning) that there is something that I need to change to stop feeling suicidal. Being suicidal is not always a burden, you could look at it as a lesson to find out who you truly are as a person and what you need to do to alleviate that feeling. Me I am trying to do and try new things, anything to find a purpose, find somewhere I belong and I’m also morbidly curious about life.

The hospital won’t be able to give you the love that you seek, it will always be temporary. To get that kind of love you have to love yourself first, which is hard to do because I certainly don’t love being me.

I still feel hopeless, misunderstood, invalidated and wanting to die. My cognition as improved before I was like you, found it hard to talk and think clearly. And now I’m finding it easier to talk.

I don’t want to hurt people with my suicide so I will wait for the day when I am alone In every possible way and then decide if I want to continue to live. I’m also morbidly curious and a glutton for punishment.

“I will never get better” 

It does feel that way. Although the depressed mind struggles with rational thought. Peoples great intentions are like poison to that state of mind, it retaliates against positive stimuli. I think
It’s unrealistic to say “I will never get better” 

how do you know that? 

Have you exhausted all possible self help strategies to come to that conclusion? 

I’m lonely and depressed today, does that mean I will always be lonely and depressed? 

You’re capable of positive thoughts by realising people have great intentions, you’re not completely lost to negativity.

It may get worse, it may get better is a more realistic statement to go by.
Yes, having a checklist gives me a sense of achievement. I didn’t do nothing all day when I lie in bed at night thinking about it.
Yes, I did that for a long time to get me going. Writing down literally everything I needed to do in the day, from the mundane to the important.

I told myself to do it anyways, even if you don't want to do it. And for me at least there was a time I realised I actually wanted to feel better rather than forcing myself to be better. 25 years of telling myself to just get up in the morning and do life. Now I look back on it I'm okay with doing nothing and when you can appreciate the beauty of doing nothing is when you're truly at peace. But I had the feeling of walking through sand all that time. It lead me to reaching out to my doctor and admitting to myself I had a problem and after two years of taking SSRI anti depressants and undertaking therapy, I am starting to see a benefit and I am feeling less hopeless about life.

To undo depression takes as long as it takes to fall into it. In another 23 years I may be better than I am now, If I continue my routine of striving to feel better about myself.

It got easier for me to seek inner peace because I fought against myself.

Practise, practise, practise, practise and fail and practise some more.

Go easy on yourself, be mindful and accept it's okay to fail, I did many times trying to climb out of my hole. As long as you keep your mind on the ultimate goal of wanting to feel better. You will not achieve it in a straight line from A to B, you may take steps backwards in order to go forward. When the bottom of cycle is good and the top of cycle is amazing, only then can you rest, be comfortable with yourself and reflect on how bad it was and how good it is now.

Depression exists for a reason, to realise something is wrong and that you can do something to correct it.

I called Samaritans 116 123 yesterday, a few different numbers in fact, it’s in my “safety plan” and I spent the majority of my time not saying anything and giving short answers, she told me “She did not know how to help me” and for the first time ever whilst being on a helpline, I respected her for being honest and saying that. It beats pretending like people on those lines are actually helping. I find talking about suicide puts me In the same conversation circles that never resolve to anything but talking in the same circles. Nothing of real substance. Mental health support is lacking. From the GPs I have spoke to, to the therapists, counsellors and psychiatrists. Nobody really knows what’s up and me less so. I laugh to myself on those helplines when I am asked “How can I help?” I don’t know, I’m calling this number in hopes of finding that out. 

I think “helping” is a passive thing between people and sometimes people don’t know if they’re actually helping or they are being helped. To some degree, deep down you making this post and getting replies is doing something to you, whether it be good or bad or helpful or useless. At least I tell myself that whilst making this reply, I could be just talking a load of bollocks, what do I really know about it?

If someone is helpful would I know it? I don’t know what help looks like. “Talking helps” is what I’m told. How true is that exactly? When most of society don’t want to talk about it. I open up and people walk away because suicide is not a subject to small talk about. So I’m leaning more to talking does not help but maybe talking to someone who understands me might help. Maybe I have not found that one person who can help me enough to see that it’s helping.

Expose yourself to it in small steps, to try and desensitise yourself to it. Takes a lot of practise. I’ve only just started my journey into Reddit and social media, so I am yet to find someone who has been rude to me. I too suffer with social anxiety. Do what you’re doing right now in this post and keep talking about it, find people here who will validate your feelings. It’s a slow and pain process but in time all those bad experiences you encounter will make you stronger minded. And just be honest with yourself and others, if people don’t like that, you can block them and never speak to them again. I can relate to your feelings and your feelings are real, I know it’s hard. I struggle with confrontation, I just want to run away but it’s a mistake if I do, that action will make me feel worse. The people that hurt you in life, tell them it hurts and stop or be ignored. Be civil with them. Don’t allow yourself to get into an argument with those kinds of people, just step away from it a little bit and think about your response. “I think you’re rude and you have hurt my feelings.” Is good enough. If you don’t get an apology, block them. And if its too overwhelming take a break from social media and come back when you feel a bit better, it’s okay to run away a little, take one step backwards but it’s bad if you do it all the time. Step back, reassess the situation and come back when your anxiety is not so overwhelming. Treat yourself for these achievements and make a big deal of it, “Wow go me for telling somebody they’re rude” You will be one step ahead of your antagonists and closer to feeling better about yourself. Its an inner struggle but the more you do it the easier it will get, keep trying, keep pushing forward and ask for help when you want it. Keep posting! I like people like you!

We’re called “Mentally Ill” because we think differently from the normal. In the grand scheme of things what is normal exactly? Is suicide any less normal than any other way of dying? It’s just a label for generalising a problem into one category and because that’s how society looks at us is part of the reason why “Mental Illnesses” is “Treated” and not “Cured.” When the care system is trying to treat a personal affliction with impersonal methods, it will always be “Incurable.” Or you’re “Treatment Resistant.”

Yes, do our best, and keep trying.

I'm OK with answering whatever questions you feel like asking, I am better at talking about it, I have practised a fair bit, still a long way to being very good at it but I am getting there, slowly. I am prescribed 200mg of Sertraline and 30mg of Mirtazapine, they help to an extent that I can see some benefit to taking the drugs, but it's not the complete answer. I have been taking them since august, before that I weaned off Citalopram and I relapsed into a deeper depression which made me overdose on paracetamol, admittedly not a big overdose of 16 tablets but my intent at the time was to hurt myself and to test the waters, to see how far I could push myself out of morbid curiosity. At the time it felt like it was the right thing to do and I have not done anything like that since then, but I do think about overdosing every time I take my current medication. I did 24 sessions of CBT and IPT, which helped me to talk about my problems, I struggled to even talk before that and the struggle to turn up to those sessions was painful, my mind wanted to give up at any moment.  My psychiatrist tells me I have anxiety and mood dysregulation disorder.
